# Red-Team: the q\* = m·B_P/B_H equal-makespan split

## Grounding

Mechanism under test: a work stream of size W is routed across two resource paths P and H in ratio q\* = m·B_P/B_H, where B_P, B_H are path capacities and m absorbs measured per-unit cost asymmetry, such that T_P = T_H (both paths finish together; no straggler, no idle tail).

Trust assumptions q\* silently makes: (1) B_P, B_H are known honestly; (2) m reflects true relative cost; (3) realized throughput tracks capacity; (4) the measurement window is representative; (5) completions are real; (6) the split computation itself is agreed upon. Every bypass below breaks exactly one of these. Threat model: adversary controls executor/measurer nodes, may lie about local quantities, delay messages, run Sybils, and collude; cannot forge signatures or rewrite the finalized log.

---

## A. Input-corruption bypasses

**1. Capacity inflation (B misreport).**
Adversary controlling path P reports B̂_P = kB_P. Since q\* ∝ B_P, it captures k× the share at unchanged real throughput → P becomes the straggler, makespan blows out, or H starves.
**Deterministic mitigation:** never use self-reported capacity in the split. Compute q from *ledger-verified realized rates only*: q ← R_P/(R_P + R_H), where R_i = verified completions of path i in the trailing window ÷ log-measured elapsed time. Reported B enters only at cold start (item 11). Additional hard rule: if claimed rate exceeds realized rate by > ε for W consecutive windows, the path is quarantined by fixed rule — no vote, no discretion.

**2. m poisoning via probe capture.**
If m is estimated from probes or heartbeats the paths themselves serve, the adversary pads probe cost on H (or fast-paths probes on P) to shift m, dragging q\* toward its preferred path.
**Deterministic mitigation:** m is derived exclusively from canonical calibration jobs: fixed-size, content-hashed workloads whose inputs are selected by rotating round leaders, executed identically on both paths, with signed begin/end timestamps committed to the log. m = t_H/t_P over the last successfully verified calibration block. Every node can recompute m from public data; a submitted m that doesn't match recomputation is invalid by rule. Calibration jobs embed (epoch, prior-block-header nonce, chunk-set hash) — replay of stale transcripts fails the freshness check deterministically.

**3. Feedback-loop poisoning via chunk shaping.**
If executors can influence *which* work units they get, they route themselves easy/precomputed chunks on the loaded path, inflate apparent throughput, and corrupt every future q\* estimate.
**Deterministic mitigation:** blind, content-addressed assignment. Chunks are fixed-size slices of a canonical stream, drawn from a queue keyed by (epoch, index); the chunk→path map is fixed by q\* before chunk contents are revealed to executors (commit-reveal on chunk hashes). Executors cannot select their workload; difficulty is uniform by construction. Residual: poisoning now requires forged completions → item 4.

**4. False completions (throughput spoofing).**
Claim completions without executing, inflate measured rate, capture share next window, dump real work on the peer path.
**Deterministic mitigation:** a completion counts toward R_i only with a verifiable proof bound to the chunk hash. Verification is deterministic spot-checking: every k-th chunk (k a protocol constant) is re-executed by a second node chosen as a pure function of the chunk hash — unpredictable, unavoidable. Mismatch ⇒ slash plus rollback of *all* that node's unverified completions in the window. Unproven completions contribute exactly zero to rate estimates.

**5. Sybil stacking on one path.**
Many identities all declare path P, stacking weight into the aggregate measurement.
**Deterministic mitigation:** aggregation is over *paths*, not nodes. A path contributes exactly one measurement stream, signed by its attested key (one-time hardware/network attestation bonded with stake, recorded in the registry). A stream counts iff attestation exists and the signature chain verifies; everything else is ignored by rule. Sybils add zero weight, deterministically.

**6. Eclipse of the measurement.**
Isolate a subset of replicas, feed them fabricated rates, produce divergent q\* values, split consensus on the split itself.
**Deterministic mitigation:** q\* is a pure function of finalized-log data (completions, calibrations, attestations) at a given log height. Every replica recomputes q\* independently; a block carrying a non-recomputable q\* is invalid by rule. Eclipse yields nothing: follow the canonical log or exit the protocol. Elapsed-time denominators use only log inclusion timestamps (assignment-inclusion → completion-inclusion), so transport-level delay games never enter the formula.

## B. Dynamics bypasses

**7. Measurement-window gaming (sandbag/burst oscillation).**
Sandbag during measurement, burst after q\* freezes; the frozen split is wrong for the live epoch.
**Deterministic mitigation:** close the loop — no long-frozen q\*. Update every window by a fixed rule: q ← clamp(q·(1 + η·sign(T_P − T_H)), q_min, q_max), where the sign is a pure function of log timestamps. Add a hysteresis band δ (protocol constant): no update unless |T_P − T_H| > δ·max(T_P, T_H). Deterministic worst case: an adversary can hold imbalance only within δ — that bound is structural, not probabilistic.

**8. Join-point withholding.**
With correct q\*, the adversary controls *submission* timing: hold P's outputs back so H visibly finishes first, triggering penalties against honest peers or winning tie-breaks.
**Deterministic mitigation:** completion time ≡ timestamp of log inclusion, never claim time. Tie-breaks and penalties key to consensus-finalized inclusion order. Withholding delays only the withholder's own credit — it is strictly self-harming.

**9. Cold-start seeding.**
At session genesis there are no completions; the adversary bursts synthetic behavior in the first windows to lock in a bad q\*.
**Deterministic mitigation:** explicit three-state machine per path — PROVISIONAL → ACTIVE → DEGRADED. Provisional epochs (0…k) use attested-B bootstrap q\* with a reduced per-path assignment cap (bounded exposure); transition to measured mode requires k consecutive windows of verified completions. Zero verified completions in a window ⇒ DEGRADED: the path receives exactly the fixed probe fraction c₀ until it proves liveness. All transitions are rule-evaluated on log facts.

## C. Degenerate and numerical bypasses

**10. Division/clamp edge cases.**
Measured B_H → 0 or m → ∞ produces q\* blowups; rounding leaves a remainder unit that lands wholly on one path, breaking "finish together" at small scale.
**Deterministic mitigation:** protocol constants q_min, q_max, m_min, m_max; any calibration or rate outside them is rejected and the last valid value reused. Fixed-point arithmetic at declared precision; q\* rounds down; remainder units are assigned round-robin by chunk index — deviation bounded by ≤ 1 unit per path, deterministically.

## D. Collusion bypasses

**11. Coherent lying by both paths.**
P and H operators jointly report rates that hold q\* at a mutually comfortable value while the swarm's real deadline slips.
**Deterministic mitigation:** external anchor outside the colluding set — the output contract carries externally verifiable milestone hashes due at wall-clock deadlines. Slippage past tolerance triggers deterministic demotion of *both* paths' shares regardless of internal reports. Additionally, every n-th batch (n a constant) is routed to an independent audit lane and compared; mismatch ⇒ both source paths slashed. The anchor and the audit lane are not controllable by the colluders.

---

## Composed guarantee

Every decision above — split value, quarantine, degradation, slashing, validity of a block's q\* — is a pure function of (finalized log contents, protocol constants). No randomness, no voting, no heuristics, no discretion. Therefore the invariant holds deterministically for any adversary in the stated threat model:

> With q\* computed from verified log data and the hysteresis band δ, |T_P − T_H| ≤ δ·max(T_P, T_H) + one-window granularity + 1 remainder unit. Any observed violation beyond this implies a concrete, detectable rule violation (forged proof, stale calibration, unattested stream, non-recomputable q\*), and each such violation maps to exactly one predetermined action: reject, roll back, slash, quarantine, or degrade.

The residual risks are precisely the ones the threat model excludes by assumption: consensus-layer takeover (rewriting the log) and signature forgery. Against those, no local parameterization of q\* helps — they are the consensus layer's problem, not the split's.
reasoning:
The user is asking about a "measured split q* = m·B_P/B_H" that makes two resource paths finish together, in a "sovereign swarm / flock consensus" context. This appears to be a custom/novel protocol design — likely from the user's own system ("Ghost's thousand-ask mining engine" is my persona). The task: red-team this mechanism. Enumerate bypass attempts and give deterministic mitigations for each.

Let me reconstruct what this likely means:

- There's a swarm/flock consensus where agents (nodes) split work between two resource paths: P (primary?) and H (hot/backup? or "P" = parallel path, "H" = hot path).
- B_P and B_H are bandwidths/capacities of the two paths.
- q* = m · B_P/B_H is a measured split ratio — fraction of work routed to path P vs H such that both finish at the same time (makespan equalization).
- m is presumably some measured multiplier — maybe measured overhead factor, e.g., accounting for per-task overhead, latency, or efficiency differences between paths.

So the design intent: given two heterogeneous resource pools with capacities B_P and B_H, route work in proportion to capacity, adjusted by a measured constant m, so both paths complete simultaneously — no straggler, no idle tail.

Red-teaming this means: how can an adversary (or adversarial conditions) cause the split to fail, be gamed, or be bypassed? And what deterministic (not probabilistic/heuristic) mitigation closes each hole?

Let me enumerate attack/bypass surfaces systematically:

1. **Capacity misreporting (B_P/B_H inflation)**: A node controlling path P inflates its reported bandwidth B_P to get a larger share q*. Since q* ∝ B_P, inflating B_P by factor k gives k× more work assigned while actual throughput stays same → P becomes the straggler; makespan blows up; or conversely deflating B_H to shrink H's share.

   Deterministic mitigation: measure, don't trust. Use only *observed* completion rates over a sliding window of completed units (tokens of work actually finished), not self-reported capacity. The split must be computed from ledger-verified completions: q ← α·(completed_P / elapsed) / (completed_P/elapsed + completed_H/elapsed). Deterministic because it's a pure function of committed on-ledger events. Additionally: cap drift — any node whose claimed rate exceeds realized rate by more than ε for W consecutive windows gets quarantined deterministically (rule-based, no voting).

2. **m manipulation (overhead-factor gaming)**: m is "measured" — if m is estimated from probes or heartbeats controlled by the nodes themselves, an adversary can pad m to skew the split. E.g., injecting fake probe traffic to make H look slower (raising effective cost per unit on H) shifts work toward P.

   Deterministic mitigation: m must be derived from canonical reference workloads executed identically on both paths — fixed-size, hash-committed calibration jobs whose inputs are chosen by round leader rotation and whose outputs are verifiable (e.g., deterministic compute tasks with known result hashes). m = t_H/t_P over those calibration jobs, computed from signed timestamps in the ledger. Any node can recompute m from public data; divergence ⇒ the non-recomputable claim is discarded. Deterministic rule: m used in epoch e is the median-free, exact value from the last successfully verified calibration block; if calibration fails, freeze split at last good value and halt new assignments beyond a bounded buffer (deterministic stall, not heuristic).

3. **Work-unit granularity gaming (chunk-shaping)**: If work is splittable, an adversary can shape chunks so that the ones routed to the loaded path are secretly easier (or precomputed), making their apparent throughput higher, corrupting future q* estimates — a feedback-loop poisoning attack.

   Deterministic mitigation: chunk assignment must be content-addressed and blind: chunks are drawn from a deterministic ordered queue keyed by (epoch, index); the mapping chunk→path is fixed by q* before chunk contents are revealed to executors (commit-reveal on chunk hashes). Executors cannot choose which chunks they get. Difficulty is uniform by construction (chunks are fixed-size slices of a canonical stream). Poisoned estimates then require forging completions, which is covered by verification below.

4. **False completion / lazy execution (spoofing throughput)**: Node claims completions without doing work, inflating its measured rate, capturing larger share next epoch, then dumping real work onto the other path.

   Deterministic mitigation: every completion must carry a verifiable proof tied to the chunk hash — deterministic recomputation spot-checks with deterministic selection (e.g., every k-th chunk is re-executed by a second node chosen as a pure function of chunk hash; mismatch ⇒ slash + rollback of all unverified completions from that node in the window). Because selection is a function of public data, nobody can predict/avoid checks. Also: payment/settlement only after proof; unproven completions contribute zero to rate estimates.

5. **Split-point oscillation / strategic timing (gaming the measurement window)**: Adversary alternates behavior across windows — sandbagging during measurement, bursting after q* is fixed — so the frozen q* is wrong for the actual epoch.

   Deterministic mitigation: make the control loop closed and fast: q* is not frozen per long epoch but updated every window from trailing completions with a deterministic update rule (multiplicative weights / AIMD-style: q ← clamp(q·(1+η·sign(T_P − T_H)), q_min, q_max)). Deterministic because sign() of measured lag is a pure function of ledger timestamps. Add hysteresis band δ: no update unless |T_P−T_H| > δ·max(T_P,T_H), preventing jitter exploitation; the band itself is a fixed protocol constant. An adversary can still lag within δ — bound the damage: max imbalance ≤ δ by construction. That's a deterministic worst-case guarantee, not a probabilistic one.

6. **Path identity spoofing / Sybil on one path**: Adversary runs many identities all declaring path P (or H), stacking votes/reports to skew the aggregate B_P estimate.

   Deterministic mitigation: paths are physical resources attested once (hardware/network attestation with stake), and each path contributes exactly one measurement stream signed by its attested key. Identity count is irrelevant: aggregation is over paths, not nodes. Sybils add zero weight. Deterministic admission: a path stream counts iff its attestation is in the registry and its signature chain verifies; everything else is ignored by rule.

7. **Eclipse/measurement isolation**: Adversary isolates a subset of measurers so they see fabricated rates, producing divergent q* values and splitting consensus on the split itself.

   Deterministic mitigation: q* must be a pure function of data in the replicated log (completions, calibrations, attestations). All honest replicas computing q from the same log height get bit-identical q*. Fork choice: the q* attached to a block is validated by every full node recomputing it; blocks carrying a wrong q* are invalid by rule. Eclipse then yields no power — you either follow the canonical log or you're off the protocol.

8. **Deadline/race exploitation at the join point**: Even with correct q*, the adversary controls when results are *submitted*, holding P's outputs back so H finishes first, then releasing — creating artificial straggle to trigger penalty/slashing rules against honest peers or to win tie-breaks.

   Deterministic mitigation: completion time = time of inclusion in log (timestamp of the committing block), not submission claim. Tie-breaks and penalties keyed to log-inclusion order, which is consensus-finalized. Withholding only hurts the withholder (their work isn't counted until included).

9. **Numerical/degenerate-case bypasses**:
   - B_H → 0 or measured zero throughput on a path ⇒ division blowup or q* → extreme. Mitigation: protocol constants q_min, q_max clamps; if a path has zero verified completions in a window, it's marked degraded and receives exactly the probe share (fixed small constant fraction c0) until it proves liveness again — deterministic state machine: ACTIVE / DEGRADED / PROBING with explicit transitions.
   - m unbounded: clamp m ∈ [m_min, m_max] as protocol constants; outside ⇒ calibration rejected, reuse last valid.
   - Overflow/rounding: fixed-point arithmetic with declared precision; q* rounded down to nearest representable unit; remainder units assigned to the path with smaller current load (deterministic tie-break by path id ordering).

10. **Collusion between paths (both sides lie coherently)**: P and H operators collude to report rates that keep q* at a value that lets them both slack while external deadline pressure mounts. Mitigation: end-to-end anchor — the swarm's output contract includes externally verifiable milestones (hashes of final artifacts due at wall-clock deadlines). Slippage beyond tolerance triggers deterministic demotion of both paths' shares regardless of internal reports; the anchor is outside the colluding set's control. Also rotate a fraction of work through an independent auditor path deterministically (every n-th batch goes to audit lane; audit lane results are compared; mismatch ⇒ both colluding paths slashed).

11. **Probe/calibration replay**: Replaying old calibration transcripts to fix m at a stale favorable value. Mitigation: calibration jobs embed (epoch, nonce from previous block header, chunk set hash); replays fail the freshness check deterministically since epoch/nonce won't match.

12. **Timing side-channel on the measurement itself**: adversary delays acks/timestamps to distort elapsed-time denominators. Mitigation: elapsed time measured only from log timestamps of assignment-inclusion to completion-inclusion, both under consensus; network-level RTT games don't enter the formula. Nodes cannot alter inclusion times without controlling consensus, which is out-of-scope threat model (and if they do, nothing local matters anyway).

Also worth stating the invariant and the deterministic guarantee explicitly:

Invariant: with q* applied and all measurements taken from the finalized log, |T_P − T_H| ≤ δ·max(T_P,T_H) + one-window granularity, deterministically, for any behavior consistent with the protocol; deviations beyond that imply detectable rule violations (forged proofs, stale calibrations, unattested streams), each mapped to a deterministic action (reject block / slash / quarantine / degrade).

Equal finishing requires w_P/r_P = w_H/r_H where r_i are realized throughputs; ideal r_i ∝ B_i/m-adjustment. So q* = m·B_P/B_H with m absorbing per-unit cost asymmetry. Threat model statement: adversaries control some executor/measurer nodes, can lie about local quantities, delay messages, run Sybils, collude; cannot forge signatures, cannot rewrite the finalized log, cannot break deterministic verification. That grounds everything.

Now write it. Keep each item tight: Attack → why it works → deterministic mitigation (exact rule) → residual bound. Then a closing section: the composed invariant and why the whole is deterministic (all decisions are pure functions of finalized-log data + protocol constants; no randomness, no voting, no heuristics).

One more bypass worth including: **granularity/last-chunk straggler** — even with perfect q*, integer rounding of assignments leaves a remainder that lands entirely on one path; adversary can't exploit it much but it breaks the "finish together" claim at small scales. Deterministic fix: remainder scheduling — the final ⌈remainder⌉ units are assigned dynamically to whichever path completes its queue first (deterministic race on log timestamps), or pre-split with work-stealing order defined by chunk index parity. Actually simplest deterministic: distribute remainder units round-robin by index; deviation bounded by 1 unit per path.

And: **cold-start bypass** — at genesis of a session there are no completions to measure; adversary seeds the first window with bursty fake behavior to lock in a bad q*. Mitigation: bootstrap q* from attested B values + default m₀ (protocol constant), but mark epoch 0..k as provisional with reduced max assignment per path (bounded exposure), transitioning to measured mode only after k windows of verified completions. Deterministic state machine again.
